currentContext.business: Larsen & Toubro operates through Infrastructure Projects (EPC of buildings & factories, transportation infrastructure, heavy civil infrastructure, power transmission & distribution, renewables, water & effluent treatment, and minerals & metals), Energy Projects (hydrocarbon onshore/offshore EPC covering oil & gas, refineries, petrochemicals and offshore wind, plus CarbonLite Solutions for power-generation BTG scope and carbon capture) and Hi-Tech Manufacturing (Heavy Engineering for process plants and nuclear energy; Precision Engineering and Systems for marine/land defence platforms, aerospace and space). Government and related entities are the primary customers (~65% of revenue), with the balance from domestic and international private-sector clients; roughly 67% of revenue is domestic and 33% international, with the GCC region (about a third of annual revenue) a particularly important market.

CarbonLite Solutions (BTG scope for power generation, carbon capture utilisation & utility packages)
Hi-Tech Manufacturing: Heavy Engineering (custom-designed critical equipment/systems for process plants and nuclear energy)
Precision Engineering and Systems (marine and land defence platforms, aerospace, space and industrial products)

currentContext.strategies: Maximising shareholder value by divesting identified non-core assets|Driving operational excellence through digital initiatives to enhance cost competitiveness|Strengthening working capital discipline and funds management|Ensuring effective and profitable execution of the robust order book|Reorganised the Hydrocarbon business into three distinct units — Onshore, Offshore and Offshore Wind — for focused execution|Consolidated data center operations under the Larsen & Toubro Vyoma brand (previously L&T-Cloudfiniti), extending core engineering and manufacturing expertise into the digital economy with emphasis on scalability, security, sustainability and responsible AI|Reallocating capital released from the Smart World & Communication divestment towards 'Engineering Intelligence', a high-growth focus area for LTTS|Investing in semiconductors through a chip-design subsidiary focused on energy, mobility and industrial applications|Advancing new business initiatives in green energy — green hydrogen and green ammonia|Funding capital needs for the real estate business, including land acquisition and development|Selective and disciplined approach to project bidding, supported by clear guardrails on sectors and geographies|Hybrid Holdco governance structure of Independent Companies (ICs) implementing the Company's strategic plan (Lakshya) with decentralised execution under Board/ECom oversight
currentContext.expansion: Project execution and commissioning milestones during FY2025-26 spanned Infrastructure, Energy and Hi-Tech Manufacturing: Phase 1 of the Navi Mumbai International Airport was inaugurated; Phase 1 of Patna Medical College & Hospital, Bihar was inaugurated (on full completion it is expected to become the world's second-largest hospital); the Residue Upgradation Facility (RUF) of 3.55 MMTPA capacity was commissioned for HPCL at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh; all facilities under the Marjan Increment Package 2 project for Saudi Aramco were energised; the Daman Upside Development Project was completed for ONGC; the BGEPIL Tapti Decommissioning Project was completed as India's first full-scale offshore decommissioning initiative; Commercial Operation Declaration (COD) was achieved for Unit-1 of the 2x660 MW SJVN thermal power plant at Buxar, Bihar and for Unit-2 of the 2x660 MW Khurja super thermal power plant, Uttar Pradesh; commercial operations began on the entire 182-TKM mainline of the Delhi-Meerut RRTS; the 112.5 MW Goaltore solar power plant in West Bengal was inaugurated as one of the largest renewable power projects in eastern India; a 156 km transmission line connecting Rooppur and Gopalganj was successfully beamed, boosting Bangladesh's energy infrastructure; HZL's Debari Roaster #6 was commissioned, expanding smelting operations; 12 Stackers and Reclaimers were commissioned; and a 1,100 TPH aggregate crushing plant was commissioned at Fujairah, UAE. Significant milestones were also achieved at the Rajasthan Atomic Power Plant (RAPP) units 7 & 8, with the Natural Draught Cooling Towers (NDCTs) and related works being executed ahead of schedule. Separately, the Indian cement industry (an end-market for the Minerals & Metals Product business) is projected to add approximately 50-60 MTPA of new capacity in FY2026-27, with further additions planned in subsequent years.

risks.risk: Credit risk in the Financial Services (L&T Finance) book
risks.note: Credit risk — transactional (default) and portfolio (intrinsic/concentration) — is described as central to L&T Finance's strategy; the retail loan book was 98% of the total loan book as at March 31, 2026, with disbursements up 38% y-o-y, meaning asset-quality outcomes are increasingly tied to rapid retail scaling.

Growing reliance on AI-driven engines (Project Cyclops for underwriting, Project Nostradamus for early-warning signals) across credit origination and portfolio monitoring means inaccuracies in these models could mis-price or mis-detect credit risk; a dedicated Model Risk Management Committee was set up to govern this exposure.

Heightened volatility in funding markets, fuelled by shifting global trade dynamics and geopolitical conflict, raises the risk of insufficient liquid assets to meet obligations, particularly for the Financial Services business.

A disruption in West Asia that began in February 2026 creates uncertainty for the global economy; India's FY2026-27 GDP growth outlook (projected at 6.9%) carries explicit downside risk from the Gulf conflict, and West Asia is a strategically important market/order source for the Group.

Increasing digitisation of business applications and algorithm-driven decisioning raises exposure to ransomware, malware and data leakage; the Board Risk Management Committee's terms of reference explicitly include evaluating cyber-security risk, and L&T Finance runs a dedicated Infosec function under an ISO 27001:2022-certified ISMS.

risks.risk: Enterprise-wide strategic, operational and regulatory risk
risks.note: The Company operates a structured enterprise risk management framework overseen by the Board Risk Management Committee, covering strategic, operational, financial, regulatory and sustainability-related risks across domestic and international operations, including market, geographical, political and reputational issues.

RBI has flagged that unsecured loans (personal loans, credit cards) accounted for 53.1% of all retail loan slippages system-wide, with private banks seeing 76% of fresh slippage from this segment, and elevated impairment among borrowers with unsecured loans from five-plus lenders amid rapid fintech credit expansion (36.1% y-o-y) — a system-level vigilance area relevant to L&T Finance's operating environment.

risks.risk: Climate risk in Rural/Farmer Finance portfolios
risks.note: L&T Finance analyses rainfall deviation and reservoir storage capacity to manage climate-linked risk primarily within its Rural Business and Farmer Finance portfolios, with climate considerations now embedded in decision-making and periodic portfolio assessments.

one-line thesis: L&T is capitalizing on India's robust public and private capex cycle and GCC infrastructure spending, with strong order inflows and a record order book, while navigating margin headwinds from input costs and supply chain disruptions; its strategic pivot into green tech and digital services offers long-term growth optionality.
financial scorecard: rev: +23% YoY; EBITDA: flat at 11.5%; PAT: +29% YoY; orderbook: Rs.3.72T; netdebt: net debt-equity 0.89
guidance: Group order inflows and revenue guidance of 12-15% (bias to upper end); Projects & Manufacturing EBITDA margin target of 9.5% for FY23, but at risk due to supply chain and input cost volatility; NWC-to-sales to end FY23 at ~20%
order book & pipeline: Rs.3.72T (record), 72% domestic, 28% international; 91% from Infrastructure & Energy; domestic breakdown: State Govt 30%, PSUs 42%, Central Govt 10%, Private 18%; international: 80% GCC, 10% Africa, 10% SEA
segment / subsidiary detail: Infrastructure: order inflows Rs.251B (+107% YoY), order book Rs.2.6T, revenue Rs.194B (+39% YoY), EBITDA margin 6.6% (-170 bps YoY); Hydrocarbon & Power: order book Rs.689B, revenue Rs.55.9B (-7% YoY), EBITDA margin 8.5% (+190 bps YoY); Defense & Heavy Eng: order book Rs.197B, revenue Rs.14.6B (-1% YoY); IT&TS: revenue Rs.101.5B (+29% YoY), margins pressured by wage inflation; Financial Services: retail book 58%, improved NIM and asset quality; Development Projects: Hyderabad Metro ridership up to 441K/day (Oct), EBITDA margin 39% (vs 13% YoY), PAT loss reduced to Rs.3.28B; Other: buoyed by Smart World & Comms, Construction Equipment
growth verticals / optionality: Green hydrogen electrolyzers (pilot operational Nov'22, JV partner selection by Mar'23); Data Centers (Panvel pilot Jan'23, Kanchipuram by Mar'24); L&T EduTech and SuFin digital platforms live and performing; TOD monetization for Hyderabad Metro; potential InvIT in Metro post-2025
margins & cost dynamics: Projects & Manufacturing EBITDA margin down 80 bps YoY to 8.2% due to job mix, close-out costs (two projects), and legacy procurement at high commodity prices; cost pressures from energy, design changes, and delayed sourcing; margin recovery expected in H2 due to favorable new procurement and project milestones
capex / expansion: No explicit group capex disclosed; implied capex focused on new businesses: Data Centers (Panvel & Kanchipuram), Green Hydrogen pilot at Hazira, battery storage (FY24); Hyderabad Metro debt restructuring via government loan and TOD monetization
capital allocation: Prioritizing debt reduction in Hyderabad Metro (target: Rs.7.5-8T from Rs.13T over 24 months via Rs.3T govt interest-free loan and Rs.2-2.5T TOD monetization); divesting non-core assets (Nabha, L&T IDPL); maintaining strong balance sheet (CRAR 22.6%, net debt-equity 0.89); reinvesting in strategic growth areas (green tech, digital)
risks & watch-items: Elevated inflation and input cost volatility; supply chain disruptions; global recession impacting IT spends; delayed state capex awards; currency depreciation; delays in divestments (Nabha, IDPL); margin slippage in fixed-price contracts; geopolitical instability in GCC
management quality / tone: Confident on India/GCC growth tailwinds and order book visibility; cautiously optimistic on margin recovery in H2; transparent about headwinds (costs, supply chain); committed to capital efficiency and ROE improvement via divestments and restructuring; avoiding overpromising on guidance
non-obvious takeaways: Hyderabad Metro's EBITDA margin of 39% is driven by operational efficiency, not revenue growth alone; ridership surge (441K/day) is a leading indicator for future cash flow stability; L&T's 85% variable-price infrastructure contracts provide natural inflation hedge; private sector order prospects up 10% YoY signals structural shift in India's capex dynamics

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
